subject: Re: MSA redlines — limitation of liability vs termination / prepaid unwind
messages:
From: Jordan Sullivan <jordan.sullivan@brightpath.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@brightpath.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA redlines — liability / termination questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightPath is excited to proceed. Our legal team attached a set of proposed MSA redlines focused on Limitation of Liability and termination remedies. Two items we want to confirm up front:

- For prepaid annual fees, we expect an explicit refund or credit mechanism on termination for convenience (pro rata for unused months).
- Wind-down assistance: we need some limited operational support (data export, routing) for up to 60 days; we'd like this to be an express obligation with fee offset.

We circled a carve-out request for gross negligence and will to discuss if that can be narrower. Please see attached: BrightPath_MSA_Proposed_Redlines_20270301.pdf.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a pro rata refund for unused prepaid fees and an express wind-down assistance obligation? Also: how do you typically reconcile LoL caps with termination refunds (does a refund count toward the LoL cap)?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Sullivan
Head of Procurement, BrightPath
--
BrightPath | jordan.sullivan@brightpath.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Sullivan <jordan.sullivan@brightpath.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — liability / termination questions

Jordan — appreciate the clear ask and the redlines. Looping in Aditya (AE) for commercial context and Monica (in-house counsel) for legal detail.

A couple quick clarifying questions so we can give a clean counter:
1) When you say "pro rata refund for unused months," do you mean a full refund less usage-based fees or a credit against future services?
2) Is the 60-day wind-down a hard requirement tied to a particular migration plan, or a maximum expectation?
3) Any required numeric caps or is BrightPath comfortable with a formulaic approach (e.g., unearned prepaid fees less amounts for services rendered)?

We can prepare a short counterproposal that preserves our LoL cap while offering a pragmatic unwind approach. Monica — any immediate redline guidance?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — liability / termination questions

(Internal) Jordan sent BrightPath's proposed redlines. Quick notes / suggested guardrails before Monica prepares language:

- Commercial: BrightPath is mid-market, strong logo. Aditya, they sign quickly but expect reasonable unwind if they prepay. Consider pro rata refund for unused months, not full fee refunds for any termination. We can trade some liquidity for a small upfront concession.
- Legal: maintain standard LoL cap (fees paid in prior 12 months) but clarify that refunds for unearned prepaid fees are excluded from "damages" calculation (i.e., they are a settlement mechanism, not an element of recovered damages). This keeps LoL meaningful while allowing refunds.
- Wind-down: propose max 30 days of assistance (BrightPath asked 60), limited to "reasonable commercially-available efforts" and capped (we should pick a dollar cap or tie to one month's prepaid fees).
- Exclusions: keep narrow carve-outs (wilful misconduct, gross negligence, IP infringement) — avoid broad carve-outs for consequential damages.

Monica — can you draft two short paragraphs we can send as a counter (one on refunds/wind-down; one on LoL interaction)? TX.

— Lauren

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — liability / termination questions

Lauren / Aditya — draft language below; I recommend we offer this as a commercial counter and reserve position in the MSA for more specific Order Form terms.

1) Refund / Unused Prepaid Fees (suggested):
"If Customer terminates this Agreement for convenience, Redwood will provide a pro rata refund for any pre-paid but unused fees applicable to the remainder of the then-current paid term, calculated on a monthly basis, less any agreed-upon costs for wind-down activities. Refunds shall be paid within thirty (30) days of effective termination."

2) Wind-Down Assistance (suggested):
"Following termination for convenience, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide up to thirty (30) days of wind-down assistance (data export, configuration handover, and reasonable runbook support). Redwood's liability for costs related to wind-down assistance shall be limited to the lesser of (a) the actual reasonable costs incurred by Redwood to provide such assistance and (b) USD 15,000, unless otherwise agreed in an Order Form."

3) LoL interaction (suggested explanatory clause):
"For clarity, any pro rata refund of prepaid fees or payments made as wind-down assistance shall not be treated as 'damages' for purposes of the Limitation of Liability. The Limitation of Liability shall otherwise remain in effect as set forth in Section X (Cap on Liability), subject to standard carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity claims."

Notes: Keep the numeric cap limited (15k) to give us a clear ceiling; if AE wants to avoid a dollar figure, we can propose 'one month's prepaid fees' instead. Also ask BrightPath to confirm they do not expect refunds to be counted toward the LoL cap.

— Monica
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Sullivan <jordan.sullivan@brightpath.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@brightpath.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — liability & termination (counterproposal)

Jordan — thanks for the detail. Attached is our counterproposal (OrderForm_Counterproposal_v3.pdf) with short, concrete language we think is commercially reasonable and preserves the Limitation of Liability while addressing BrightPath's unwind concern. Key points:

- Pro rata refund for unused prepaid months (refund within 30 days).
- 30 days of wind-down assistance, limited to 'commercially reasonable efforts' and capped at USD 15,000.
- Express clarification that refunds and wind-down payments are not 'damages' for LoL purposes; the LoL cap otherwise remains as negotiated.

We've provided the counter via DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/embedded-signature/abc123-BP-2027 — please review and sign within 5 business days if acceptable. If BrightPath prefers a different cap (e.g., one month's prepaid fees), let us know and we can consider.

Attached: OrderForm_Counterproposal_v3.pdf

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through language.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Sullivan <jordan.sullivan@brightpath.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@brightpath.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — liability & termination (counterproposal)

Lauren / team — thanks for the clear counter and the DocuSign link. A few small requests from our side before signature:

1) Instead of an express USD cap, can we make wind-down assistance 'limited to a customer's actual reasonable costs up to a maximum equal to one (1) month of prepaid fees' — this ties the ceiling to our spend and avoids negotiating a fixed dollar amount.
2) Confirm that the LoL carve-outs remain narrow and that IP indemnity and willful misconduct are unaffected by your proposed clarification.

Assuming language on (1) is adjusted as above and the IP carve-out is confirmed, we can sign the updated Order Form today. I've routed to our Contracts team and attached our signed acknowledgment of the counter (signed_redline_brightpath.pdf).

Jordan Sullivan
Head of Procurement, BrightPath
